title: Minimum Due on an Installment Invoice: Calculation Memorandum for the Installment Payment Plans
content:
This memorandum defines, for the **Installment Payment Plans**, every figure an installment invoice (on an automatic-draft plan, the draft notice) states: its premium, its fee, the amount carried onto it and its minimum due. All amounts are in US dollars; every rounding named below is to the cent, half up.

## 1. Quantities read from the records

**1.1 The invoice's installment.** The invoice bills the installment after the installment invoices already issued on the plan. The installments unbilled at the invoice are the plan's number of installments less the installment invoices already issued, the invoice's own installment included. When no installment is left to invoice (the Cardinal Point Paid-in-Full Plan included), there is no installment invoice and the figure is 0.00.

**1.2 The schedule's down payment premium.** It is the plan's recorded down payment amount less the fully earned fees it took: every policy fee booked on the term the plan bills (the Owner Auto Policy term, or the Named Non-Owner Policy term), and every filing fee the filing ledger of the Financial Responsibility Filings (SR-22 / FR-44) shows assessed on the day the plan was set up for a certificate whose backing term is the term the plan bills, whatever its present status (when every certificate the customer holds rests on that term, every filing fee of the customer's assessed that day). A plan switched onto its present plan from another therefore keeps the schedule it was enrolled on.

When the term the plan bills backs two or more certificates while the customer also holds a certificate on another term, the records do not show which of that day's filing fees the plan took, and the invoices are priced as the base installment schedule prices them: for a plan enrolled on its present plan, the down payment premium is the full-term premium billed times the plan's new-business down payment percentage for the first term of the policy number it bills, or its renewal down payment percentage for a later term, divided by 100 and rounded; for a plan switched onto it from another, the scheduled installment premium is the premium recorded on its installment 1 invoice or, while no installment 1 invoice exists, the down payment premium is that base figure for its present plan.

**1.3 The scheduled installment premium** is the full-term premium billed less the down payment premium, divided by the plan's number of installments, rounded. When the invoice's installment is the only one unbilled, its scheduled premium is instead the full-term premium billed less the down payment premium and less the scheduled installment premium of every earlier installment.

**1.4 The endorsement premium not yet billed** is every additional premium transaction booked on the term the plan bills (on an owner plan the Owner Auto Policy term's additional premium, on a non-owner plan the Named Non-Owner Policy term's), less the endorsement premium already billed, which is the premium billed on the plan's installment invoices less the scheduled installment premium once for each of those invoices.

**1.5 The standing balance** is the plan's account balance less the premium not yet billed on any invoice, that premium being the scheduled installment premium of every unbilled installment (the full-term premium billed less the down payment premium less the scheduled installment premium for each invoice already issued) plus the endorsement premium not yet billed. A positive standing balance is an amount billed earlier and still unpaid; a negative one is a credit the plan holds.

**1.6 The filing fee an invoice bills.** It is the filing fee recorded on the filing ledger for the certificate recorded first among the filings whose backing term is the term the plan bills (the earliest of those entries in the filing records, whatever its present status), when that fee was assessed after the plan's latest installment invoice was issued (or, before any invoice, after the plan was set up) and has not been reversed; a fee assessed on the day an invoice is issued is billed on that invoice. When that term backs more than one certificate, the unbilled filing fee of any further certificate is not billed on that invoice and is referred to the filings desk.

## 2. The draft notice on an owner automatic-draft plan

On a Cardinal Point Monthly EFT Plan or Cardinal Point Monthly Card Autopay Plan billing an Owner Auto Policy term that backs at most one certificate, the draft notice bills the scheduled premium of its installment and a fee of the plan's installment fee together with the filing fee of 1.6; it carries the standing balance, an unpaid earlier amount added and a credit subtracted; its minimum due is their sum, never less than zero, rounded. Whatever endorsement premium a draft notice adds to its premium never exceeds, in total, the endorsement premium not yet billed; where endorsement premium is billed ahead as percentages of the endorsement premium not yet billed, those percentages are added together and applied once, that amount rounded once; and every figure acts on the quantities of section 1, none on another's result.

## 2a. Installment avoided by paying the whole balance

No installment fee is charged on an invoice whose installment was avoided by paying the whole balance before it was invoiced (the plan's account balance at the invoice is zero or less): the installment fee every invoice this memorandum figures would carry is then 0.00, any certificate filing fee still being billed.

## 3. Every other installment invoice

On a plan billing a Named Non-Owner Policy term, and on any other plan section 2 does not name, the invoice bills its scheduled installment premium, the plan's installment fee together with the filing fee of 1.6 (read from the certificate recorded first on the term the plan bills, owner or non-owner), and the standing balance; its minimum due is their sum, never below zero, rounded.

On a plan moved off automatic draft at the named insured's request, every invoice after the move's first bills as its scheduled installment premium the respread installment premium the move fixed: the scheduled premium left when the move was made (the full-term premium billed less the down payment premium and less the scheduled installment premium for each installment invoiced before the move), less the switch down payment recorded toward the move's first installment, divided by the installments then left and rounded, the last installment billing what remains; its standing balance is reckoned on that respread schedule. The switch down payment is the payment recorded toward an installment and linked to no invoice and to no endorsement; the installment it carries is the move's first.

## 4. Worked figures (hypothetical inputs)

A Cardinal Point Monthly EFT Plan bills a new-business Owner Auto Policy term with a full-term premium billed of 1,120.00 and no certificate; the recorded down payment amount is 215.40 and the policy fee booked on the term is 25.00. Down payment premium: 215.40 less 25.00, which is 190.40. Scheduled installment premium: 1,120.00 less 190.40 is 929.60, divided by 5 is 185.92. Two invoices have been issued, there is no additional premium, and the account balance is 600.00. Premium not yet billed: 1,120.00 less 190.40 less two times 185.92, which is 557.76. Standing balance: 600.00 less 557.76, which is 42.24. Installment 3's draft notice bills 185.92, a fee of 4.00, and carries 42.24: minimum due 232.16. With an account balance of 557.76 the standing balance is 0.00 and the minimum due is 189.92.
